prompt: Why are you interested in this role?
variants: What attracted you to this position?
Why did you apply?
intent: Checks that you understand the job and have a specific reason, not a generic one.
answerGuide: Name two parts of the job description that match work you have already enjoyed doing.
Back each with a short piece of evidence from your history.
Tie it to what the team needs.
followUps: Which part of the role excites you most?
Which part do you expect to be hardest?
What else are you considering?

prompt: Why do you want to work here?
variants: What do you know about our company?
Why this company and not another?
intent: Looks for real research and alignment, not flattery.
answerGuide: Mention a specific product, customer type, or value you learned from their site, posts or job ad.
Connect it to your experience or interest.
Show you understand their market or challenge.
followUps: What do you think our biggest challenge is?
Who are our competitors?
How did you hear about us?

prompt: What do you know about our product or the customers we serve?
variants: Have you used our product?
What do you think we do well?
intent: Checks whether you researched the product and customers beyond the home page, and can say what problem the product solves.
answerGuide: State what the product does and who uses it in a sentence or two.
Add one observation or question that shows thought.
Admit gaps honestly and say what you would want to learn.
followUps: What would you improve?
Who do you think our users are?
What would you want to learn first?

prompt: Why are you leaving your current role, or why did you leave your last one?
variants: Why did you leave?
What made you start looking?
intent: Checks for red flags such as bitterness, conflict, or unreliability.
answerGuide: Give a short, honest, neutral reason (role ended, contract, seeking more scope).
Say something positive about what you gained.
Pivot to what you want next and why this role.
followUps: Would you go back?
What would you have changed?
How did your manager see it?

prompt: Where do you see yourself in five years?
variants: What are your career goals?
Where do you want to be down the road?
intent: Checks ambition that fits the company and whether you are likely to stay.
answerGuide: Describe growth in skill and scope, not just a title.
Make it plausible within this path (for example deeper analysis, product ownership or customer ownership).
Connect early years to learning and contributing here.
followUps: What skills do you need to get there?
What if this role does not lead there?
What are you doing now to prepare?

prompt: Why are you choosing this career path now?
variants: What made you decide to go into this field?
Why did you shift toward this type of work?
intent: Looks for a coherent reason for choosing this career direction now, based on work you have done rather than a sudden whim.
answerGuide: Identify what you enjoyed most in past work (translating, structuring, testing, helping).
Show steps you took to move in this direction.
State what you want to do next.
followUps: When did you decide?
What did you try first?
What would make you change your mind?

prompt: What motivates you at work?
variants: What gets you out of bed in the morning for work?
What kind of work energizes you?
intent: Wants intrinsic motivation consistent with the job.
answerGuide: Name one or two real drivers (solving problems, helping users, mastering a craft).
Back with a moment when you felt it.
Tie to the job's daily work.
pitfalls: Contradicting the role (for example hating routine in a routine-heavy role).
followUps: When were you most motivated?
What drains you?
How does this role fit?

prompt: What kind of team or culture helps you do your best work?
variants: Describe your ideal work environment.
What type of manager do you work best with?
intent: Checks whether the conditions you work best in (clear priorities, written communication, feedback) fit this team's reality.
answerGuide: Describe working conditions truthfully (clear priorities, written communication, feedback).
Give an example of a good fit from your past.
Show flexibility.
pitfalls: Listing conditions the company clearly lacks.
followUps: What type of environment is hard for you?
How do you adapt?
What did your best manager do?

prompt: Why did you choose the roles you did so far?
variants: Walk me through the decisions in your career.
How did you end up where you are?
intent: Tests whether your choices so far show a thread and agency, and whether you can describe what each taught you.
answerGuide: Give a thread: what each step taught you.
Be honest about luck and planning.
Land on the present decision.
followUps: What was the best move?
What would you not do again?
What is the common thread?

prompt: Why are you interested in working remotely?
variants: Why do you want a remote role?
What draws you to remote work?
intent: Checks that your reasons are about the work style and not avoidance.
answerGuide: Give a work-based reason (focus, written communication, flexibility to deliver).
Give evidence from past remote or independent work.
Acknowledge how you stay connected to the team.
pitfalls: Reasons about avoiding people or the commute only.
followUps: What do you find hard about remote work?
How do you stay connected?
Would you travel or go in occasionally?

prompt: What are you looking for in your next role?
variants: What matters most to you in a new job?
What would make this the right job for you?
intent: Checks that what you want next (ownership, learning, a real product) is something this role actually offers.
answerGuide: State 2 or 3 priorities: learning, ownership, a real product, a good team.
Link them to this role.
Avoid compensation as the first thing.
followUps: What is non-negotiable?
What would make you leave?
What would be a dealbreaker?

prompt: What do you think makes someone successful in this role?
variants: What qualities does this job demand?
How would you measure success in the first year?
intent: Checks your understanding of the job's real demands.
answerGuide: Name 3 qualities tied to the posting (accuracy, communication, curiosity).
Give a one-line example of each in your own work.
Add what you would want to learn from them.
followUps: Which of those is your strongest?
Which is weakest?
What would a great first 90 days look like?

prompt: What are you doing to prepare for a move into this field?
variants: What have you done to build the skills for this role?
How have you been developing yourself?
intent: Demonstrates initiative and honest skill level.
answerGuide: List 2 or 3 actions: self-study, projects, tools practice.
Be honest about level (intermediate, basic, learning).
Say what is next.
followUps: What was the hardest to learn?
What can you do now that you could not before?
What is next?

prompt: Where would you like to grow within a company like ours?
variants: What growth paths interest you?
What would you like to be doing in two or three years?
intent: Tests realistic growth ambitions inside the company and whether you plan to stay long enough to contribute.
answerGuide: Name the skills and responsibilities you want to expand.
Show you understand the paths in this kind of company.
Link the first year to learning the product well.
followUps: What would you need from us?
What if growth is slower than expected?
What skill would you build first?

prompt: What is the most important thing to you in a job: pay, growth, team, or mission?
variants: Rank what matters to you in a job.
intent: Reveals your top priority among pay, growth, team and mission, and whether it conflicts with what the role provides.
answerGuide: Answer honestly with one top priority and a reason.
Show others also matter.
Make sure it does not conflict with the role.
followUps: Why that one?
What would you trade?
What did you give up before?

prompt: How does this role fit with your long-term plans?
variants: Is this a stepping stone or a destination?
intent: Checks commitment: whether this role fits your next several years and you are not using it as a short stop.
answerGuide: Show the role as a real step with learning to gain.
Mention how you will contribute for the long term.
Avoid sounding like you will leave soon.
pitfalls: Saying it is just a stepping stone.
followUps: How long do you hope to stay?
What would keep you here?
What would make you leave?

prompt: Why healthcare, or why this industry?
variants: What interests you about this domain?
Why this sector?
intent: Tests genuine, informed interest in healthcare or the industry, including awareness of its pressures such as compliance and urgent staffing.
answerGuide: Give a personal or academic link to the field.
Show awareness of its pressures (compliance, urgent staffing, patient impact).
Tie your skills to a need.
followUps: What do you find hard about the industry?
What trends do you follow?
How does your degree help?

prompt: What would you do if you did not get this job?
variants: What is plan B?
What happens next if we pass?
intent: Tests resilience and sincerity: what you would do if turned down, which shows how much you want this specific job.
answerGuide: Say you would be disappointed and continue pursuing similar roles.
Mention you would ask for feedback.
Reaffirm the interest in this role.
followUps: Would you apply again?
What would you do differently?
What else is on your list?

prompt: What are you looking for in a manager?
variants: How do you like to be managed?
intent: Checks whether your expectations of a manager (clear priorities, regular feedback) are workable and show you take ownership.
answerGuide: Describe 2 things: clarity on priorities and regular feedback.
Give an example of what helped.
Show you take ownership.
pitfalls: Wanting a micromanager or none at all.
followUps: What did your best manager do?
How much check-in do you want?
What did you find hard in a past manager?

prompt: What does success look like to you in your first year here?
variants: What would you want to accomplish in your first year?
intent: Tests realistic first-year goals you would commit to and how you would measure them.
answerGuide: Set learning goals first, then contribution goals.
Make 2 or 3 concrete outcomes.
Invite feedback on what the team would define as success.
followUps: How would you track that?
What would you do in month three?
What do you need from us?

prompt: What attracts you to entry-level work given your experience?
variants: Are you overqualified for this role?
Why apply for an associate-level job after managing a project?
intent: Checks flexibility and whether you will stay engaged.
answerGuide: Explain the fit: you want the specific craft and a stable team, not a title.
Show you are willing to do the detail work.
Emphasize growth and contribution.
pitfalls: Sounding like you will be bored.
followUps: Would you accept direction from someone with less experience?
What would you want to learn?
What if the job stays the same for a year?

prompt: You could apply to QA, business analysis, product and support roles. Why this one?
variants: Why this role and not a similar one?
intent: Tests focus: someone applying everywhere needs a reasoned preference and an honest account of the overlap in your work.
answerGuide: Name the strand of your past work most like this role, with one example.
Say why that strand energises you.
Mention you are open to adjacent roles but this is a first choice.
Link to what the team is doing.
followUps: What if we offered another role?
What parts of this role worry you?
Where do you want to be in two years?

prompt: You have worked at a very small company. Why do you want a bigger, more structured one (or the reverse)?
variants: How will you adapt to our size?
intent: Tests whether you understand the trade-offs between small and large teams and have realistic expectations.
answerGuide: Name what the small company gave you: breadth, ownership and speed.
Name what you want to learn: depth, process, mentors.
Show you understand the change: slower decisions, narrower scope.
Give an example of adapting.
followUps: What will you miss?
How do you handle bureaucracy?
What are you worried about?

prompt: What would make you leave this job after six months?
variants: What are your deal-breakers?
intent: Reveals expectations and whether the role matches them; answer with specifics and no ultimatums.
answerGuide: Name genuine issues: dishonesty, no learning, role very different from what was described.
Show you would raise concerns before leaving.
Keep it short and calm.
Do not list trivial preferences.
followUps: Have you left a job for that?
What would you do first?
How do you raise concerns?

prompt: In a final values round: what about our mission matters to you personally?
variants: Why does our mission matter to you?
intent: Final-round values check: specific, credible link between your history and the company's purpose.
answerGuide: Pick one part of the mission and say why it matters, drawing from your experience with healthcare staffing or customers.
Give evidence: a moment from work.
Connect to the work you would do.
Avoid copying their website.
followUps: Where do you disagree with us?
What would you change?
How will you contribute to the culture?

prompt: If you get two offers, how will you choose?
variants: How are you weighing opportunities?
intent: Reveals decision criteria and your honesty about alternatives.
answerGuide: Name 3 criteria: learning, the team and manager, role content, compensation.
Say this role's strength against them.
Be honest without bluffing.
Say what you need to know to decide.
followUps: Where do we rank?
What would tip the decision?
Do you have a deadline?

prompt: You have been a project manager. Why customer success (or support) instead of staying in project work?
variants: Why change direction toward customers?
intent: Tests a sideways move: a coherent reason grounded in what you enjoyed.
answerGuide: Say what you enjoyed most: liaising with customers, documentation, solving their problems.
Give evidence from past work.
Show you understand the role is different: ongoing relationship, retention measures.
Express what you want to build.
followUps: What do you miss about project work?
How will you handle sales pressure?
Where does this lead?

prompt: Why do you want healthcare administration support after working in software?
variants: How do software and healthcare meet for you?
intent: Tests sincerity and fit for a healthcare operations role, using your pharmacy staffing experience.
answerGuide: Link your last role to healthcare operations: emergency pharmacy staffing and the people it serves.
Say what you want from the new role: closer to patients' outcomes, process work.
Show you understand the pace and compliance demands.
Link your health science degrees.
pitfalls: Saying you want a change only.
followUps: Why not clinical work?
How do you handle sensitive information?
What do you know about our organisation?

prompt: Where do you want to be in three years, and what would you do here to get there?
variants: What is your career plan?
intent: Checks realistic growth tied to the role and no sign you will leave in months.
answerGuide: Give a direction rather than a title: deeper in analysis and product, or customer outcomes.
Link to steps in this role.
Name skills to build.
Show you want to stay long enough to contribute.
followUps: What if the path doesn't exist here?
What would you need from us?
What skills?
